value.hook: Open before removing, adding or rate-checking any daemon process launch (ps, lsof, tmux, omp, git), or answering a performance seat's cost questions
value.title: Daemon launch work: what can be read in-process, and how to find why a launch fires

sections.name: body
sections.value:
- Attribute a launch before fixing it. `pij-rs --json ping | jq .data.registrations.by_key` splits register attempts by purpose with their `ps` cost. In #85, 187 of 229 `ps.registration-native-process` launches came from `heartbeat.pane.unchanged` (Copilot extension re-registrations), about 2.5 per registration: one argv read per host-named ancestor (copilot, node). Take two `.data.spawns.by_op` readings a known interval apart. A quiet fleet can show 0 in 120 s.
- In-process reads available today, without unsafe: `pij_harnesses::proc` gives `parent_of`, `parent_and_name` (macOS short BSD info, any process), start time (`observed_start`), and Linux `/proc` stat/exe/cmdline.
- NOT available on macOS without unsafe:
  - argv (`KERN_PROCARGS2`);
  - a whole-process list;
  - a TCP peer pid (`LOCAL_PEERPID`/`SO_PEERCRED` are Unix-socket only, and proc_pidinfo 0.1.4 has no socket fd info).
  Those launches stay; say why.
- Tap attach counts are per PANE, not per session. They are paid once per live pane at daemon start (process-local tracking is empty) plus repairs. 144 meant about 140 panes, not a loop.
- Sensor: `spawn_sites.rs::no_daemon_launch_names_a_program_bare` refuses any `Command::new("x")` literal without a `/` in daemon crates. System tools go by absolute path (`/bin/ps`, `/usr/sbin/lsof`); user tools go through `pij_core::program::launch`. Record every retired op in `retired_launches_stay_retired`.
- Linux socket holders can't be proven absent. A `/proc/<pid>/fd` census misses threads after the leader's `pthread_exit`, SCM_RIGHTS in flight, other fd tables, and pid namespaces. Ruled (R299-001): the sweep's Linux holders are always unknown.
- Process uid: a socket file takes the binder's filesystem uid, so classify by effective+filesystem uid, never "any uid matches". A process of the runner's own user can still be non-dumpable (fd links EACCES), and CI hits it.
- When `bash` launches are under test, macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2 imports `UID` from the environment while bash 5 doesn't. Write tests that probe which one is running.
